Re: Flora Macdonald

https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=VF90m2C853k&pp=ygUXTmF0YWxpZSBmbG9yYSBtYWNkb25hbGQ%3D

This is yet another AMAZING, and unexpected, ‘slow air’ version of this tune--but with a jazz twist. I mean… I hope more people out there hear this. I hope this arrangement is appreciated in the world! I think it’s Grammy worthy. Seriously. One of Natalie MacMaster’s finest moments; Flora MacDonald as a slowed-down, jazz-inspired ballad. So much variation, subtlety, interesting counterpoint & accompaniment of just the piano, guitar & double bass. It’s ethereal but also somewhat “lost”-sounding, like almost apathetic or disillusioned. Natalie starts the track with just the standard setting of the tune (maybe a bit Nata-fied). Then, the second time through, she gets down a little more, and then it peaks & crescendos, before a calming piano bridge… then she revisits the CCDD parts of the tune again, only slightly more embellished, melodic variations with interesting staccato bowing, open E/fourth finger double-stops. The whole track ends with a very melancholy minor chord. Her variations are just so full of emotion!!

↳ Posted by Erik-Fiddler on February 23rd, 2023.

Flora Macdonald, X:6

This was my take on Natalie MacMaster’s slowed down, bluesy-jazz version. A very ethereal, melancholy, almost “lost” vibe to it. It’s only fiddle, Brad Davidge on guitar, with a (upright?) bass and piano, and no other instrumentation. Stripped down and acoustic, and played considerably slower. Natalie does a lot more variations, frequent droning double-stops with the open-E and fourth-finger E on the A-string, plus it’s a great showcase of her signature staccato bowing. Overall an awesome track and arrangement.

↳ Posted by Erik-Fiddler on January 8th, 2024.

Re: Flora Macdonald

Thanks for this. This tune, played by Natalie, is easily my favorite piece of trad, period, and it would be in my top 10 of any genre. The plaintive, haunting sound, the building tension, release and re-building tension is utterly engaging.

I’ve been working on it for mando for some time. The first 2/3 is easy to memorize, the last third, not so much. When I get that down, it will be time to figure out how to incorporate the non-Flora intro.
